# hamclock-next

**Maintained SDL2 rewrite of HamClock — grey line, propagation, DX cluster**

- **Version recorded:** 1.5
- **Categories:** `hf-propagation`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/k4drw/hamclock-next>
- **Supersedes:** `esphamclock`

## What it does

Displays a live world map with the grey line, solar and geomagnetic indices, satellite passes, DX cluster spots and band-condition predictions, either full-screen on a dedicated display or in a window.

## Why you would want it

It is the at-a-glance station dashboard for deciding which band to work, and it is one of two maintained continuations of HamClock, whose author became a Silent Key in January 2026. The other is OpenHamClock, which has the larger community; which should be the recommended default is Q-006.

## Before it will work

A working network connection and a reachable data backend. Set your latitude, longitude and callsign on first run.

## How it installs

- source (cmake) from https://github.com/k4drw/hamclock-next/archive/refs/tags/v1.5.tar.gz
  - build dependencies: `patch`, `libsdl2-dev`, `libsdl2-ttf-dev`, `libsdl2-image-dev`, `libcurl4-openssl-dev`, `libsqlite3-dev`, `cmake`, `build-essential`

Binaries this produces:

- `hamclock-next`

## Known problems

Widely reported in mid-2026 to have stopped working after the original author's death. Tested 2026-08-25: hamclock.com is up and serving version 4.27. The host that is gone is clearskyinstitute.com. This manifest defaults to the Open HamClock Backend, a community-run alternative, and the endpoint is a configurable field rather than a string compiled into a launcher script — so switching backends is a one-line change, not a rebuild.

## Keeping it current

- probe: github release (`k4drw/hamclock-next`)
- strategy: rebuild
